memory_candidates.content: In POPLmark-style cofinite-quantification encodings of eigenvariable rules (`boxI`/`diaE` with `∀y∉L, P y` premises), the encoding gives equivariance/weakening 'for free' only when the cofinite family is BUILT via a uniform swap-invariant construction (introduction direction). It does NOT give, for free, a way to RECOVER a cofinite family from a single instance obtained via an existential/choice-based argument (a Zorn-maximal element, or a per-branch induction hypothesis with no shared witness) -- this is the elimination/reflection direction, and it fails whenever the 'already covered' portion of the label space (e.g. a Zorn-maximal context's domain) is unboundedly large: a swap transport for a label already entangled in existing structure is not merely unproven but ACTIVELY INVALID (it corrupts the existing structure's edges under the swap). Three plausible-seeming shortcuts (finite-subgraph existential redefinition of the consequence relation, direct reuse of a per-branch induction hypothesis without relabelling, and a 'bounded old-label' special case) were tested against this exact shape of problem and all reduce to the identical uniform-index-across-an-unbounded-family obstruction. The only known fix is a step-indexed/well-founded construction carrying a 'only ever adjoin fresh labels' invariant through every step -- ordinary Zorn's-lemma existence results (e.g. Mathlib's zorn_le0) do not expose enough structure to state or prove this invariant after the fact.

reflection.what_worked: Reading Simpson's raw proof text (chunk_0102.md/chunk_0103.md) in full, rather than relying on the prior handoffs' characterization, surfaced the exact one-line justification Simpson gives ('otherwise we could derive... by an application of (◇E)') that the transcription had to formalize -- confirming the obstacle is genuinely in the transcription gap between a terse paper proof and a fully mechanized cofinite-quantification encoding, not a missed technique. Testing concrete alternative fixes (finite-subgraph Deriv, direct IH reuse, bounded old-label case) to formal conclusions, rather than re-stating the difficulty abstractly, produced a genuinely sharper diagnosis than the two prior handoffs.
reflection.what_was_hard: Distinguishing 'this specific shortcut fails' from 'no shortcut of this general shape can work' required constructing concrete failure arguments (e.g. showing the naive swap corrupts H.G's existing edges at an old label, not just 'is unproven') rather than asserting difficulty.
reflection.what_was_missed: Did not attempt implementing even a scoped-down conditional lemma (e.g. the 'bounded-old-label' special case sketched but not formalized) due to time/effort budget -- this would have been a legitimate, if narrow, piece of real Lean progress and is flagged as a possible small follow-up if a future dispatch wants SOME sorry-free artifact from this investigation.
reflection.successes: Produced a diagnosis materially sharper than the two prior handoffs (three additional shortcuts formally ruled out, not just re-asserted difficulty), landed as real file content (probe docstrings + plan paragraph, not just a handoff), and gave a concrete, appropriately-scoped recommendation (a new dedicated planning effort) rather than either falsely claiming closure or vaguely re-deferring with the same description the mission explicitly prohibited.
